summary: Corporate SSID: GPO network auth rate-limit deployment causing EAP-MSCHAPv2 failures for SF office
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 08:40 PT, multiple employees in SF office reported inability to join corporate SSID (CorpSecure). Symptoms: client prompts for credentials repeatedly then times out. Immediate impact: ~30% of office unable to access internal services, raised to internal Slack #it-support. Initial hypothesis: RADIUS/NPS rejects after new Group Policy Object (GPO) deployment that enforces a per-user authentication rate-limit. This ticket tracks troubleshooting, temporary mitigation and rollout of permanent fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect to CorpSecure SSID on a Windows 11 corporate laptop with domain account.
3) Observe repeated credential prompts or 'Authentication failed' event after ~15 seconds.
4) Repeat with another device or macOS device to compare behavior.
logs: wpa_supplicant (macOS) debug: EAP: TLS/PEAP handshake completed, inner EAP method result: 'failure'
NPS server log excerpt (nps.log 2026-03-12T08:41:02): Reason-Code 0x19 (Access-Reject) - 'EAP inner method failed - user exceeded auth rate limit'
Netsh trace on gateway: dropped packets to RADIUS server when concurrent_auth_limit reached
Recent GPO change: 'NetworkAuthRateLimit' policy set to '5 attempts per minute' deployed to OU=SF-HQ at 2026-03-12 07:55 PT (GPO change id: GPO-20260312-9)
investigation_notes: 07:58 IT push: security team applied new baseline (NetworkAuthRateLimit) to SF-HQ OU to combat brute-force attempts; rollout targeted 150 machines.
08:15 First tickets came in; NPS servers reported spike in Access-Rejects with 'rate limit'
08:22 Reproduced failure on a patched Windows 11 test machine. Clearing cached credentials allowed single auth but subsequent attempts were rejected for ~12s.
08:45 Confirmed NPS setting 'MaxAuthPerUser=5/min' (intended to be 60/min). GPO parameter mismatch suspected (units misinterpreted between GPO UI and NPS template).

09:05 Engineering checked NPS cluster: NPS policy enforced correctly, but secondary RADIUS proxy returned rate-limit metrics due to duplicate auth bursts from endpoint roaming and background network noise.
09:30 Temporary mitigation applied: GPO rollback to previous NetworkAuthRateLimit=disabled for SF-HQ OU via emergency GPO reversal (change id GPO-20260312-9b).
10:00 Observed drop in Access-Rejects and successful re-auths across test devices.
comments: Aisha Patel (IT): 'Ticket opened after Slack reports from #it-support. Collecting affected hostnames and users. Pls escalate to infra.'
Marco Li (Network Eng): 'Confirmed NPS logs showing rate-limit rejections. Suspect GPO units mismatch. Will coordinate rollback.'
Jonas Müller (Security): 'Rate limiting was intended for perimeter hosts only — my bad on scope. Need to review GPO targeting and MDM translation.'
Marco Li: 'Rolled back GPO at 09:30, monitoring. Please validate on a few previously-failing machines and report results.'
User feedback (Lina Gomez): 'I can now connect and my calendar started syncing. Thanks.'
Follow-up (Marco): 'Next steps: update GPO template to use seconds units, add NPS telemetry guardrails, schedule controlled redeploy to non-office OUs only.'
resolution: Temporary rollback of NetworkAuthRateLimit GPO to previous state restored connectivity. Permanent fix: update GPO parameter to correct units (set to 60 attempts/minute), add scoping filter to exclude client machines from aggressive per-user limits, and deploy NPS guard script to alert when per-user rate limit spikes. Change will be implemented via change request CR-2026-0314 and staged to a canary group before global rollout.
